point_types.name: Definite integral expression with correct limits
point_types.earns: A definite integral whose limits match the requested interval and whose integrand matches the requested quantity, with or without the differential (sg-26:4, sg-22:2, sg-24:4).
point_types.does_not_earn: An unsupported numerical value, or a definite integral whose bounds are wrong (sg-22:18); an ambiguous response where the initial value sits inside the integral rather than beside it (sg-24:4).
point_types.notation_requirements: Differential may be omitted; sg-22:2 accepts dx written for dt. sg-23:8 treats a missing differential as recoverable for this point but restricts later eligibility.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: Independent of other points in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-22:18 states a definite integral with incorrect bounds earns neither this point nor the answer point; sg-22:8 states a definite integral with incorrect limits is not eligible for the answer point; sg-24:4 states that if the limits of integration are incorrect the response does not earn the answer point, and that a response containing any linkage error can earn at most two of the three points in the part.
point_types.notes: This family absorbs what would otherwise be a separate limits-of-integration family. Limits are scored inside the integral point or inside the answer point, never as a point of their own.

point_types.name: Integrand only, limits assessed elsewhere
point_types.earns: A correct integrand inside an integral, whether or not the limits and outside constants are right (sg-25:7, sg-26:19).
point_types.does_not_earn: An integrand built from the wrong function, or an integrand presented with no integral sign (sg-25:7).
point_types.notation_requirements: Differential optional (sg-25:7, sg-25:14). sg-26:19 requires the limits to be numerical but not correct.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-25:7 states the limits and the factor one half are assessed in the answer point, not in the integrand points.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-25:7 special case: an indefinite integral with a correct integrand loses the r-squared point, earns the integrand point, and stays eligible for the answer point.

point_types.name: Antiderivative
point_types.earns: A correct antiderivative of the presented integrand, with or without the constant of integration (sg-25:14).
point_types.does_not_earn: An antiderivative of the wrong form, or a jump from integral to value with no antiderivative shown (sg-26:18).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-25:14 and sg-26:20 both state the answer point requires this point first.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-23:17 allows an antiderivative of the right form with a wrong constant to earn this point while blocking the answer point; sg-21:11 keeps u-substitution work with unconverted limits eligible for this point.

point_types.name: Answer with or without supporting work
point_types.earns: The correct value on its own, with no supporting work required (sg-25:3, sg-26:4).
point_types.does_not_earn: A value outside the accepted precision, or a value inconsistent with a required earlier step where the rubric imposes one.
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: A reported decimal answer must be accurate to three places after the decimal point, rounded or truncated; at most one point per question is lost to inappropriate rounding (sg-25:2, sg-26:2). sg-26:4 also accepts a stated rounding to the nearest integer and several truncations.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: Independent of other points in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-25:3 treats incorrect or unclear communication between the integral and the answer as scratch work, so bad linkage does not cost this point.

point_types.name: Answer with supporting work or setup shown
point_types.earns: The correct value together with the setup the prompt demanded, such as a difference and a quotient from a table or an equation that produces the value (sg-26:2, sg-25:4).
point_types.does_not_earn: An unsupported value (sg-23:10, sg-22:9), or a setup with no value (sg-26:2).
point_types.notation_requirements: sg-22:6 withholds this point for an equation of the form function equals constant, such as a derivative expression set equal to a number without evaluation.
point_types.precision_rules: A reported decimal answer must be accurate to three places after the decimal point, rounded or truncated; at most one point per question is lost to inappropriate rounding (sg-25:2, sg-26:2).
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: Independent of other points in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-26:11 banks this point once a correct unsimplified expression appears, so later simplification errors do not remove it.

point_types.name: Units
point_types.earns: Correct units, whether or not they are attached to a numerical value (sg-25:11, sg-26:2); equivalent compact forms such as birds per day squared are accepted (sg-26:2), and sg-24:2 also accepts a shortened unit name attached to a numerical value.
point_types.does_not_earn: Units with no value present at all; sg-24:2 states a response that presents only units without a numerical approximation does not earn the point, and sg-22:13 says the same.
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-22:13 allows the units point with an incorrect approximation but not with no presented value.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.notes: Units are scored only where the prompt asks for them. sg-21:11, sg-22:15 and sg-22:16 state units are not required and are not read in those parts, and sg-26:4 states units are not considered in scoring.

point_types.name: Interpretation of an accumulated quantity with units and interval
point_types.earns: A sentence naming the accumulated or averaged quantity in context together with the time or spatial interval (sg-26:3, sg-23:2, sg-24:3).
point_types.does_not_earn: An interpretation that omits the interval, or that restates the integral without naming the quantity (sg-26:3); an interpretation carrying incorrect units, which sg-24:3 states forfeits the point even though units are not otherwise required.
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-26:3 states this point can be earned whether or not the sum and approximation points were earned.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.notes: sg-26:3 says the response need not include units of time or the location name, so the unit demand varies by year. sg-24:3 makes the asymmetry explicit: units need not be referenced, but incorrect units in the interpretation lose the point.

point_types.name: Interpretation of a derivative value in context with units
point_types.earns: A sentence giving the rate of change of the named quantity, its value, its units, and the instant it applies to (sg-21:3, sg-23:4).
point_types.does_not_earn: An interpretation whose sign language contradicts the presented value, such as decreasing at a rate of a negative number (sg-23:4).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-23:4 and sg-21:3 both require some presented numerical value for the derivative before this point is available.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.notes: Only two rubric instances in the documents read, so tagged single-source.

point_types.name: Interpretation of an integral as an arc length over an interval
point_types.earns: Naming the integral as the arc length or the length of the graph of the given function, and naming the interval it is taken over; the rubrics split these as two points (sg-24:16). sg-24:16 also accepts distance explicitly connected to the graph, such as distance along the curve.
point_types.does_not_earn: A bare reference to distance or distance travelled with no connection to the graph, which sg-24:16 states does not earn the arc length point although it stays eligible for the interval point; a reference to the length of a different function (sg-24:16).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-24:16 keeps the interval point available after the arc length point is lost, and requires the interval to be connected to arc length, length, or distance.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.notes: One document in the corpus read, and its wording comes from the OCR layer sg-24 page 16, so tagged single-source.

point_types.name: Justification by sign analysis of a derivative
point_types.earns: A statement that the derivative is positive on one side and negative on the other, closed by a global claim about the whole interval (sg-25:5, sg-25:9).
point_types.does_not_earn: A local argument only, such as a bare First or Second Derivative Test with no statement that the critical point is the only one on the interval (sg-25:5, sg-22:12).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-25:5 and sg-25:9 keep the answer point available to a response that fails this point with a local or incorrect global argument.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-22:12 states that a local argument must also state the critical point is the only one, otherwise the justification point is lost while the answer stands.

point_types.name: Justification by candidates test
point_types.earns: A global argument that evaluates the function at every interior critical point and at both endpoints, with the evaluations correct to the stated precision (sg-25:5, sg-25:19).
point_types.does_not_earn: A candidates table missing an endpoint (sg-23:15), containing an evaluation error (sg-23:15), or listing extra x-values (sg-25:19).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: sg-25:5 and sg-25:9 require candidate evaluations correct to the first digit after the decimal, rounded or truncated; sg-22:5 allows up to three decimals or correctly rounded integers.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-25:19 allows candidate values to be imported from an earlier part, and lets the answer point follow the imported values.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-22:5 states a correct justification earns its point even when the answer point is lost to a decimal presentation error.

point_types.name: Classification of a critical point by a derivative test
point_types.earns: Correct classification of the critical point as a relative maximum, relative minimum, or neither, with analysis using a first or second derivative test; the test need not be named (sg-26:8).
point_types.does_not_earn: A candidates test, which sg-26:8 states is not sufficient justification here; an assertion with no supporting sign or second-derivative analysis. sg-24:10 states the classification point cannot be earned without the preceding sign point and is earned only for a correct justification with the correct classification.
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-26:8 requires the critical-value point first, and does not require the value to be restated here; sg-24:10 requires the sign point first.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.notes: sg-23:13 accepts the shorter form that the derivative does not change sign, so neither extremum occurs. sg-24:10 accepts a sign statement at a single value on each side of the critical point and states it is not necessary to say the derivative does not change sign on those intervals, and lists a Second Derivative Test alternative.

point_types.name: Considers the derivative set equal to zero
point_types.earns: Presenting the equation derivative equals zero, or an equivalent equation, or discussing the sign change of the derivative, or using the phrase critical points of the function (sg-25:5, sg-26:17).
point_types.does_not_earn: Presenting only the solved critical value, which sg-25:5, sg-25:9, sg-26:17 and sg-25:19 all state is not sufficient.
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-22:5 states a response that misses this point is still eligible for the remaining points of the part.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-22:12 gives the point to a response that isolates the single critical number without writing the equation explicitly.

point_types.name: Considers the sign of a derivative
point_types.earns: An explicit statement about whether a first or second derivative is positive, negative, or zero on the relevant interval, symbolically or in words (sg-26:12, sg-24:8, sg-24:10).
point_types.does_not_earn: A statement about the sign of the function rather than the derivative, or a reference to the concavity of the derivative itself (sg-26:12).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-26:12, sg-24:8 and sg-24:10 all make the following reason or justification point eligible only after this point is earned.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.notes: sg-24:8 awards this point for the equation, either inequality, or even the solved critical value, which is looser than the parallel consideration points at sg-25:5 and sg-26:17.

point_types.name: Differentiable implies continuous
point_types.earns: An explicit statement that the function is continuous because it is differentiable, or an equivalent chain from twice differentiable through differentiable to continuous (sg-25:12, sg-26:5, sg-22:14).
point_types.does_not_earn: A bare statement that the function is continuous with no justification (sg-25:12, sg-26:5).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-25:12 and sg-26:5 state the response does not need this point to be eligible for the conclusion point, and sg-26:5 lets a response that earned it skip restating continuity.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.

point_types.name: Intermediate Value Theorem conclusion
point_types.earns: Showing the target value lies strictly between two function values, stating the function is continuous, and answering yes (sg-25:12, sg-26:5).
point_types.does_not_earn: A bare yes with the theorem named, which sg-26:5 states is not sufficient; a naming of the wrong theorem (sg-25:12).
point_types.notation_requirements: sg-22:14 rejects a bracketing statement that lists the two endpoint values without saying the target lies between them, but allows that response to recover the conclusion point.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: Independent of other points in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-25:12 and sg-26:5 both state the theorem need not be named, but a named theorem must be the correct one.

point_types.name: Mean Value Theorem or Rolle conclusion
point_types.earns: A correct average rate of change together with a statement of differentiability on the open interval and continuity on the closed interval, and a yes (sg-23:3, sg-21:17).
point_types.does_not_earn: An appeal to the Intermediate Value Theorem, which sg-23:3 states cannot earn the conclusion point here.
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-23:3 requires the difference point first; sg-21:17 instead allows the conclusion point with a correct setup but an incorrect or missing evaluation.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.notes: Both documents state the theorem need not be named provided the hypotheses and conclusion are given. Rolle is accepted as an alternative in sg-23:3.

point_types.name: Form of a Riemann or trapezoidal sum
point_types.earns: A sum whose terms each show a value factor and a width factor, with at least five of the six factors correct for three subintervals (sg-25:13, sg-26:3, sg-23:2) or seven of eight for four subintervals (sg-22:15).
point_types.does_not_earn: A left or right sum where a midpoint or trapezoidal sum was asked for (sg-26:3, sg-25:13); an unsupported total (sg-26:3, sg-22:15, sg-24:3).
point_types.notation_requirements: sg-25:13 and sg-26:3 instruct readers to read an equals sign as approximately equal for this point.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: Independent of other points in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-25:13 and sg-26:3 state any single incorrect factor blocks the approximation point while the form point can still stand; sg-25:13 and sg-26:3 both give the form point but not the value point to a completely correct sum of the wrong type, and sg-24:3 gives one of the two points for the same situation.
point_types.notes: sg-24:3 adds that values must be pulled from the table to earn the approximation point, and that units will not affect scoring for it.

point_types.name: Approximation value supported by the sum
point_types.earns: The numerical value of the sum with the supporting products present (sg-25:13, sg-23:2).
point_types.does_not_earn: The value alone with no work (sg-26:3, sg-22:15, sg-23:2).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-25:13 requires the form point before this point; sg-26:3 explicitly allows this point without the form point, for example from a correct sum of products.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-25:13, sg-26:3 and sg-23:2 all bank this point once a correct unsimplified sum appears, so later arithmetic slips do not remove it.

point_types.name: Average value formula
point_types.earns: The definite integral over the interval together with evidence of division by the interval length; a correct answer alongside a correct integral counts as that evidence (sg-25:3, sg-26:9).
point_types.does_not_earn: An integral with the wrong integrand, such as the derivative in place of the function (crabbc-25:3); a formula divided by the wrong length (sg-22:3).
point_types.notation_requirements: Differential optional (sg-26:9). The formula may be presented in one step or across several (sg-25:3, sg-22:3).
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: Independent of other points in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-25:3 and sg-26:9 treat incorrect linkage between integral and answer as scratch work; sg-23:4 is stricter and takes one of two points for the same pattern, which is a year-to-year change in treatment.

point_types.name: Average rate of change expression
point_types.earns: An expression showing both a difference of function values and a quotient by the difference of inputs, or its correct value (sg-26:2, sg-25:11).
point_types.does_not_earn: A bare quotient template with no values substituted (sg-25:11, sg-26:2); the solved value alone where the prompt demanded the setup (sg-25:4).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: sg-22:13 and sg-21:17 do not require simplification, but any simplification presented must be correct.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: Independent of other points in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-25:4 lists several equivalent forms, including an integral of the derivative over the interval divided by the length.

point_types.name: Product rule
point_types.earns: A differentiation that correctly applies the product rule to the given expression (sg-25:20, sg-22:16).
point_types.does_not_earn: A response that treats one factor as constant, which sg-22:16 states is eligible for the chain rule point but not this one.
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-22:16 states the product rule and chain rule points may be earned in either order and that the answer point requires both.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-25:21 allows a quotient rule applied to a separated-variables solution to stand in for the product rule.

point_types.name: Chain rule
point_types.earns: Correct differentiation of the inner function, including the required differentials (sg-22:16, sg-25:21).
point_types.does_not_earn: A product rule written without one or both differentials, which sg-22:16 states earns the product rule point but not this one.
point_types.notation_requirements: sg-22:16 treats a missing differential as the defining failure for this point.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-25:21 keeps the value point available to a response that earns the chain rule point but not the product rule point, provided the substitution is consistent.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.

point_types.name: Derivative of an accumulation function by the Fundamental Theorem
point_types.earns: Writing the derivative of the accumulation function as the integrand evaluated at the variable, in general or at the requested value (sg-25:16, sg-24:13, sg-24:15).
point_types.does_not_earn: Differencing the integrand at the two limits, which sg-25:16 states earns the answer point but not this one; equating a variable expression to a numerical value, which sg-24:15 states earns at most one of the two points in that part.
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-25:16 allows the answer point on an implied application of the theorem even when this point is not earned, and sg-24:13 states the same in its own wording.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.notes: sg-24:13 requires the connection to be made explicitly in that part, and states that writing the second derivative relation instead earns this point but restricts how the following reason point can be earned. sg-24:14 states a response with one or more linkage errors does not earn the first point it would otherwise have earned.

point_types.name: Tangent line approximation
point_types.earns: An approximation computed from a line through the given point whose slope is the declared derivative value (sg-23:10).
point_types.does_not_earn: An unsupported approximation (sg-23:10); an approximation simplified incorrectly (sg-23:10).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-23:10 makes the approximation point contingent on a nonzero slope declared as the derivative value.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-26:11 states presentation of a tangent line equation is not considered in scoring for the slope point, and banks the slope point once an unsimplified correct expression appears.

point_types.name: Over or underestimate decided from concavity
point_types.earns: Citing the sign of the second derivative or the concavity of the graph, and concluding that the tangent line lies above or below the curve (sg-23:10, sg-26:12).
point_types.does_not_earn: An argument from concavity at a single point (sg-23:10, sg-26:12); a reference to the concavity of the derivative rather than of the function (sg-26:12).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-26:12 states eligibility for this point requires the sign-of-second-derivative point first; sg-23:11 allows it with an incorrect second derivative provided that expression is a nonconstant linear function negative over the relevant range.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.notes: sg-24:4 carries the same architecture for a rate-of-change question: the point is earned only for a correct answer with a correct reason referencing the sign of the second derivative, a reason from evaluation at a single point does not earn it, an ambiguous pronoun does not earn it, and the interval need not be restated.

point_types.name: Higher derivative expression evaluated at a point
point_types.earns: A correct expression for the second or higher derivative, evaluated at the requested point, consistent with the earlier derivative work (sg-25:20, sg-23:10).
point_types.does_not_earn: An expression left in terms of the first derivative where the prompt asked for it in terms of the dependent variable (sg-23:11).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-25:21 ties eligibility to the product and chain rule points and permits a consistent value from a partially correct expression.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-25:21 states a correct unsimplified substitution earns the point regardless of later simplification errors.

point_types.name: Separation of variables
point_types.earns: Rearranging the differential equation so each variable sits with its own differential, in the form constant times the dependent differential over the dependent expression equals constant times the independent differential (sg-26:13).
point_types.does_not_earn: Any attempt that leaves both variables on the same side; sg-26:13, sg-23:12, sg-21:20 and sg-19:5 all state that without separation the entire part scores zero.
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: This point gates every later point in the part (sg-26:13, sg-23:12, sg-21:20).
point_types.eligibility_after_error: sg-21:20 states that if an error in separation leaves one side correct, only the matching antiderivative point remains available; sg-26:13 gives a special case where a sign error in the denominator keeps the constant point but blocks the solve point; sg-24:11 gives a special case where an incorrect separation earns neither the separation point nor the solve point but stays eligible for both antiderivative points and, through them, the constant point.
point_types.notes: Scope marked BC_only because the AP Calculus BC differential equation questions carry the BC-only header in sg-26:12, although separable equations themselves are shared content.

point_types.name: First antiderivative in a separated equation
point_types.earns: One consistent antiderivative, either the logarithmic side written with parentheses or absolute value, or the independent-variable side (sg-26:13).
point_types.does_not_earn: An antiderivative inconsistent with the separated form (sg-26:13).
point_types.notation_requirements: sg-26:13 accepts either parentheses or absolute value on the logarithm; sg-23:12 states an antiderivative written without absolute value symbols stays eligible for all points; sg-21:20 and sg-24:11 accept either form, and sg-24:11 states explicitly that a logarithm written without absolute value symbols earns that antiderivative point.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: Requires the separation point (sg-26:13).
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.

point_types.name: Second antiderivative in a separated equation
point_types.earns: A second consistent antiderivative, so that both sides of the separated equation are integrated (sg-26:13).
point_types.does_not_earn: A single antiderivative with the other side left unintegrated (sg-26:13).
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.
point_types.dependency_on_other_points: sg-26:13 awards this point only when two consistent antiderivatives are present. sg-23:11 collapses the two antiderivative points into one, which is a year-to-year structural difference.
point_types.eligibility_after_error: No eligibility restriction stated in the rubrics reviewed.

point_types.name: Constant of integration used with the initial condition
